---
name: 1mcp
description: "Use when the user wants to aggregate, unify, or unify-gateway many MCP servers behind one runtime, or mentions \"1MCP\", \"1mcp\", \"@1mcp/agent\", \"one MCP to rule them all\", \"聚合 MCP\", \"统一 MCP\", \"一个 MCP 管 N 个\", \"MCP 网关 / MCP gateway\", \"MCP 代理 / proxy\", \"MCP preset / filter / tags\", or managing MCP server inventory across clients (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, etc.). Also Use when the user mentions URLs: https://github.com/1mcp-app/agent or https://docs.1mcp.app, or when an AI agent session is flooding context with too many MCP tools and needs progressive discovery or lazy-loading to reduce token usage. Covers installing via npm (`npm i -g @1mcp/agent`), `1mcp serve` aggregated runtime, `1mcp proxy` stdio mode for broad client compatibility, CLI mode for progressive tool discovery (`instructions`/`inspect`/`run`), MCP server inventory (`1mcp mcp add/list`), presets (`1mcp preset`), per-project `.1mcprc` config, auth profiles (`1mcp auth`), cli-setup hooks for Codex/Claude, template servers with context variables ({project.*}/{user.*}/{environment.*}), and common flags (transport, filter, preset, lazy-loading, async-loading, config-reload, OAuth 2.1)."
---

# 1mcp - one MCP server to aggregate them all

`@1mcp/agent` (npm) provides the `1mcp` CLI - a unified MCP runtime that
aggregates many MCP servers behind one process, with progressive discovery,
presets, filtering, proxy mode, and per-project context.

- Repo: https://github.com/1mcp-app/agent
- Docs: https://docs.1mcp.app
- npm:  https://www.npmjs.com/package/@1mcp/agent

## When to use this skill

Trigger this skill when the user's intent matches any of:

- Aggregate / unify many MCP servers behind a single runtime (`1mcp serve`).
- Reduce per-client MCP wiring and per-session tool/token bloat.
- Add progressive discovery for agent loops: `instructions -> inspect -> run`.
- Manage MCP server inventory shared across Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, etc.
- Configure per-project `.1mcprc` (preset/filter/tags/context), template servers.
- Expose one stdio bridge (`1mcp proxy`) for clients that only speak stdio.
- Secure the aggregate runtime with OAuth 2.1 and tag-based scopes.

Common natural-language triggers (en/zh): "aggregate MCP servers",
"one MCP to rule them all", "1MCP", "1mcp", "@1mcp/agent", "MCP gateway",
"MCP proxy", "MCP preset/filter", "reduce MCP tools / token usage",
"聚合 MCP", "统一多个 MCP", "一个 MCP 管多个", "MCP 网关", "MCP 代理".

## When NOT to use this skill

- A single upstream MCP server, optionally with direct `.mcp.json` wiring.
- Wiring an AI client to one MCP server by name (use that client's native config).
- Debugging one MCP server itself (use that server's docs/issues).
- HTTP-only clients that already speak MCP and want no project context - those
  can attach directly to `1mcp serve` over streamable HTTP.

## Golden rule

**Start `1mcp serve` once, then drive it from the tools below.** The serve
process is the aggregated runtime (the Aggregated Runtime in 1MCP's own
domain language); everything else (`proxy`, `instructions`, `inspect`,
`run`, clients) talks to that runtime. Do not spawn a fresh server per request.

## Requirements

Node >= 18. Verify with `1mcp --version` (e.g. `0.34.4`) and the full contract
with `1mcp --help` (flags may change between releases - re-run for authoritative
list).

## Install / update

```bash
npm install -g @1mcp/agent      # global install exposes the `1mcp` bin
1mcp --version                  # confirm installed
# update:
npm install -g @1mcp/agent@latest
```

If the `1mcp` bin is not on PATH after install, check `npm bin -g` and add it
to PATH, or run via `npx @1mcp/agent <args>`. This skill assumes the local
npm install path; verify with `Get-Command 1mcp` (PowerShell) or
`which 1mcp` (sh).

## The mental model

```
+-------------------+        +----------------------------------+
|  AI clients       |  stdio |  1mcp proxy  (stdio bridge)      |
| (Claude/Codex/    |------->|  - reads .1mcprc project config  |
|  Cursor/others)   |        |  - resolves preset/filter/tags    |
+-------------------+        +--------------+-------------------+
                                            | HTTP
                                            v
                             +----------------------------------+
                             |  1mcp serve  (aggregated runtime)|
                             |  - hosts static + template servers|
                             |  - presets, filters, auth, lazy   |
                             |  - exposes instructions/inspect   |
                             +----------------------------------+
```

Approach matrix (pick the one that matches the client):

| Approach                | Best for                                | Tradeoff                                              |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| **1MCP CLI mode**       | Codex, Claude, agent loops              | Needs a running `1mcp serve` instance                |
| **1MCP stdio proxy**    | Max compatibility across clients        | Still depends on `serve`; HTTP clients have direct path|
| **Direct streamable HTTP** | MCP-native HTTP clients              | No project context, no `.1mcprc`, broader surface     |
| Custom proxying         | One-off shims                           | You own discovery, filtering, auth, lifecycle          |

## Quick start (3 commands)

```bash
npm install -g @1mcp/agent
1mcp mcp add context7 -- npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp   # register a server
1mcp serve                                              # shell 1: runtime
```

In a second shell, use CLI mode against the running serve:

```bash
1mcp instructions                                       # what's loaded + flow
1mcp inspect context7                                   # server overview
1mcp inspect context7/query-docs                        # one tool's schema
1mcp run context7/query-docs --args '{"libraryId":"/mongodb/docs","query":"aggregation pipeline"}'
```

For agent wiring (one-time), prefer the installer helper rather than hand-edits:

```bash
1mcp cli-setup --codex
# or, repo-scoped for Claude Code:
1mcp cli-setup --claude --scope repo --repo-root .
```

For a given agent, choose one mode only. If you switch that agent to CLI mode,
remove its old direct MCP configuration first.

## Run 1mcp as a long-lived daemon (auto-start on boot)

For agent-style deployments you want the Aggregated Runtime (`1mcp serve`) to be
always up so any client (Codex, opencode, Cursor, Claude, your own scripts) can
attach on demand. Two recommended options, plus the `--background` fallback:

### Linux / macOS: systemd unit

```ini
# /etc/systemd/system/1mcp.service
[Unit]
Description=1MCP aggregated runtime (@1mcp/agent)
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/usr/bin/env 1mcp serve --transport http --host 127.0.0.1 --port 3050 \
  --enable-async-loading --async-min-servers 4 --async-batch-notifications \
  --enable-config-reload --config-reload-debounce 300
ExecReload=/bin/kill -HUP $MAINPID
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

Before registering the task, download and extract the SEA exe:

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://github.com/1mcp-app/agent/releases/latest/download/1mcp-win32-x64.zip" -OutFile "$env:TEMP\1mcp-win32-x64.zip"
Expand-Archive -Path "$env:TEMP\1mcp-win32-x64.zip" -DestinationPath 'C:\tools\1mcp' -Force
```
### Windows: Task Scheduler (scheduled task)

Recommended: use the official installer with the SEA exe (no Node module resolution on the cold path):

```powershell
# Point -BinaryPath to the extracted 1mcp-win32-x64.exe; the script
# handles action/trigger/settings/runlevel and post-boot verification notes.
.\scripts\install-windows-task.ps1 -BinaryPath 'C:\tools\1mcp\1mcp-win32-x64.exe'
```

Equivalent minimal inline form (kept for machines where the script is unavailable):

```powershell
$exe = 'C:\tools\1mcp\1mcp-win32-x64.exe'
$logfile = 'C:\Users\Administrator\AppData\Roaming\1mcp\logs\server.log'
$argStr = 'serve --transport http --host 127.0.0.1 --port 3050 ' +
  '--config-dir "C:\Users\Administrator\AppData\Roaming\1mcp" ' +
  '--enable-async-loading --async-batch-notifications --enable-config-reload --config-reload-debounce 500 ' +
  '--log-level error --log-file "' + $logfile + '"'

$action  = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute $exe -Argument $argStr -WorkingDirectory 'C:\tools\1mcp'
$trigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -AtStartup
$settings = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -AllowStartIfOnBatteries -DontStopIfGoingOnBatteries `
  -ExecutionTimeLimit ([TimeSpan]::Zero) -RestartCount 5 -RestartInterval (New-TimeSpan -Minutes 2) `
  -StartWhenAvailable -MultipleInstances IgnoreNew
$trigger.Delay = 'PT30S'  # boot trigger delay
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName '1mcp-daemon' -Action $action -Trigger $trigger -Settings $settings `
  -RunLevel Highest -Force

# Post-boot verification:
#   schtasks /query /tn '\1mcp-daemon' /fo LIST /v   # LastResult must be 0
#   Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 3050 -State Listen # must list the exe PID
#   Invoke-WebRequest http://127.0.0.1:3050/health/ready -UseBasicParsing | Select StatusCode
```

DO NOT use a VBS wrapper (`wscript.exe ... daemon-hidden.vbs`) for this task: it leaves no console
window for log capture, cannot relay exit codes, and bypasses the official script path. The exe
is the first-class Windows distribution (`1mcp-win32-x64.exe` in each GitHub release).

IMPORTANT: the user-scope `server.pid` file is what `1mcp proxy` reads to discover the daemon.
Because you pinned ONE_MCP_CONFIG_DIR to the user scope above, the Task Scheduler daemon and any
user-spawned `1mcp proxy` (from Codex / opencode / Cursor) read and write the *same* pid file.
No symlink, no shared state across scopes. On cold boot the daemon writes server.pid first;
any client proxy spawned later just follows that file to the right PID.

### `--background` quick fallback (no service manager)

```bash
1mcp serve --background \
  --enable-async-loading --async-min-servers 4 --async-batch-notifications \
  --enable-config-reload
1mcp --status   # or 1mcp --stop / 1mcp --restart
```
Detached but not registered with the OS service manager - fine for dev, not for
boot-persistence.

### Why `--enable-async-loading` is the default recommendation

Without it, `1mcp serve` uses legacy synchronous loading and waits for ALL
configured MCP servers to connect before opening the HTTP port. With 10 backends
that cost ~12 s of "no listeners yet" on every restart. With
`--enable-async-loading --async-min-servers 4` the HTTP port opens within ~100 ms
and the remaining backends come online in the background, advertising themselves
via `listChanged` notifications (batched by `--async-batch-notifications`).
Pair with `--async-timeout <ms>` for the initial wait window,
`--async-notify-on-ready` to push per-server readiness, and
`--async-batch-delay <ms>` to tune notification batching.

## Top-level commands

| Command              | Purpose                                                         |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `1mcp serve`         | Start the aggregated HTTP runtime (the core). Default command. |
| `1mcp proxy`         | Start a stdio proxy bridging clients to a running `serve`.      |
| `1mcp mcp`           | Manage MCP server configs (`add`/`list`/`remove`...).            |
| `1mcp preset`        | Manage server presets for dynamic filtering.                     |
| `1mcp auth`          | Manage authentication profiles (OAuth 2.1) for secured serve.  |
| `1mcp app`           | Manage desktop-application MCP configurations.                 |
| `1mcp cli-setup`     | Install 1MCP CLI hooks/ref files for Codex or Claude.          |
| `1mcp instructions`  | Show CLI-mode instructions for agents using a running serve.    |
| `1mcp inspect`       | Inspect a server or a `server/tool` from a running serve.        |
| `1mcp run`           | Run one MCP tool against a running serve.                       |
| `1mcp registry`      | Manage MCP-registry operations.                                 |

## `serve` flags worth knowing

(Subset of `1mcp --help`; run it for the full list.)
Use these when starting the runtime. Defaults are good for a quick start.

```bash
1mcp serve \
  -t http                 \
  -P 3050                 \   # port (_http)
  -H 127.0.0.1            \   # bind host
  -f "web AND database"   \   # advanced filter expression
  --preset "my-preset"    \   # server preset
  --enable-lazy-loading --lazy-mode metatool       \  # ~95% fewer tokens
  --enable-async-loading --async-min-servers 2    \  # non-blocking startup
  --enable-auth                                  \  # OAuth 2.1 (or --auth, deprecated)
  --enable-scope-validation                       \  # tag-based scopes
  --enable-config-reload --config-reload-debounce 300 \  # hot-reload on file change
  --log-level info --log-file ./1mcp.log
```

Lifecycle helpers (operate on the selected Runtime Scope, then exit):

- `1mcp --background`      - start the runtime detached (a long-lived daemon).
- `1mcp --stop`           - stop the runtime in scope.
- `1mcp --restart`        - stop + fresh restart.
- `1mcp --status`         - report current runtime state and exit.

> Warning Background daemon note: launching long-running servers from a
> bash tool is not reliable (child processes are reaped on command exit). Prefer
`--background` (detached), or run `1mcp serve` in a real terminal.

### Logging & global request timeout

- `--log-level error` only sets the boot level. MCP clients send `logging/setLevel`
  on connect (requestHandlers.js) and can raise it back to `info` at runtime — expect
  that, don't chase it. Rotation bounds the damage.
- File rotation (`maxSize`/`maxFiles`) is **not** a CLI flag; it comes only from the
  `[logging]` block in `config.toml` (loggingConfig.js). e.g.:
  ```toml
  [logging]
  level    = "error"
  maxSize  = "100m"   # winston maxsize, in-place rotation
  maxFiles = 5
  ```
- Global request timeout fallback: put it in `mcp.json` `serverDefaults` — merged into
  every server that doesn't set its own `requestTimeout` (mcpConfigMerge.js):
  ```json
  { "serverDefaults": { "requestTimeout": 300000 } }   // 5 min fallback
  ```
  The default SDK timeout is 60 s; slow stdio backends (semgrep, agent-browser) hit it
  and 1mcp reports `unknown-ID` / `-32001 Request timed out` per unknown request.

### Lazy-loading (token savings)

`--enable-lazy-loading` exposes a small set of meta-tools; real tools are
loaded on demand (~95% token reduction). Modes:

- `metatool` - 3 meta-tools only (smallest surface)
- `hybrid`   - direct tools + meta-tools (use `--lazy-direct-expose <globs>` to white-list direct tools)
- `full`     - lazy disabled

Related: `--lazy-preload`, `--lazy-preload-keywords`, `--lazy-inline-catalog`,
`--lazy-cache-max-entries`, `--lazy-cache-ttl`, `--lazy-fallback-on-error skip|full`,
`--lazy-catalog-format flat|grouped|categorized`, `--lazy-fallback-timeout`.

### Async loading (non-blocking startup)

`--enable-async-loading` lets servers come online in the background while the
runtime already accepts requests. Pair with `--async-min-servers <n>`,
`--async-timeout <ms>`, `--async-batch-notifications`, `--async-batch-delay <ms>`,
`--async-notify-on-ready`.

### Session persistence & notifications

`--enable-session-persistence` (default on), `--session-persist-requests`,
`--session-persist-interval`, `--session-background-flush`,
`--session-storage-path`. Capability updates push to clients via
`--enable-client-notifications` (default on). Internal MCP management tools
are off by default: `--enable-internal-tools` / `--internal-tools` to opt in
(discovery, management, safe categories).

### Auth (OAuth 2.1)

```bash
1mcp auth <subcommand>     # manage profiles (profile name, tokens, etc.)
1mcp serve --enable-auth   # newer flag (preferred; --auth is deprecated)
```

Pair with `--enable-scope-validation` for tag-based scopes, and
`--rate-limit-window`/`--rate-limit-max`, `--session-ttl` for quotas.
Use `--trust-proxy` and `--health-info-level full|basic|minimal` for
deployment hardening.

## Per-project config: `.1mcprc`

Place `.1mcprc` (JSON5, comments allowed) in the project root. The proxy
command reads it to set **default connection settings** for that project.

Schema: https://docs.1mcp.app/schemas/v1.0.0/project-config.json.

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://docs.1mcp.app/schemas/v1.0.0/project-config.json",
  // Priority: preset > filter > tags (only one will be used)

  // Option 1 (highest priority): name a preset
  "preset": "my-preset",

  // Option 2 (medium): boolean filter expression
  // "filter": "web AND database",

  // Option 3 (lowest): tags - array or comma-string
  // "tags": ["web", "api", "database"],
  // "tags": "web,api,database",

  // Context-aware proxy mode: enables template substitution
  "context": {
    "projectId":   "my-awesome-app",
    "environment": "development",
    "team":        "platform",
    "custom": {
      "apiEndpoint":  "https://api.dev.local",
      "featureFlags": ["new-ui", "beta-api"],
      "debugMode":    true
    },
    "envPrefixes":   ["MY_APP_", "API_"],
    "includeGit":    true,
    "sanitizePaths": true
  }
}
```

### Template variables (only when `context` is set)

Use these in MCP server `command`/`args`/`env`:

| Category        | Variables                                                                     |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Project         | `{project.path}` `{project.name}` `{project.environment}` `{project.custom.*}` |
| Git             | `{project.git.branch}` `{project.git.commit}` `{project.git.repository}`        |
| User            | `{user.username}` `{user.name}` `{user.email}` `{user.home}`                   |
| Environment     | `{environment.variables.*}`                                                     |
| Context/session | `{context.path}` `{context.timestamp}` `{context.sessionId}` `{context.version}`|

Default with fallback: `{project.git.branch?:main}`.

Template functions: `| upper`, `| lower`, `| capitalize`, `| truncate(n)`,
`| replace(from,to)`, `| basename`, `| dirname`, `| extname`,
`| default(value)`, e.g. `{project.name | upper}-{context.timestamp | date('YYYY-MM-DD')}`.

## Client wiring (Codex / Cursor / opencode / Claude / agent loops)

1MCP exposes the Aggregated Runtime in two complementary ways:

- **stdio proxy** - the client spawns `1mcp proxy` as a child process that bridges
  the client's stdio MCP interface to the running `1mcp serve` over Streamable
  HTTP. This is what almost every agent IDE uses (Codex, opencode, Claude Code),
  because they only speak stdio MCP. It also carries `.1mcprc` project context
  (preset/filter/tags/template vars) through `_meta.context`.
- **Direct streamable HTTP** - MCP-native clients (Cursor, Claude with `mcp add -t http`)
  attach straight to `http://127.0.0.1:3050/mcp?app=<client>`. No project context,
  broader tool surface exposed directly.
- **CLI mode** - no MCP wiring; the agent shell uses `1mcp instructions / inspect / run`
  against the running serve. Works even in sessions that failed to spawn a proxy
  (see "Session visibility" below).

Pick ONE per client; do not double-attach. A single `1mcp serve` instance serves
all of them concurrently.

### Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`)

Install via the helper (writes hooks + ref files) **and** register the stdio MCP:

```toml
# 1) one-time hook install (agent discovers tools via 1mcp instructions/inspect/run)
#    run in your shell: 1mcp cli-setup --codex

# 2) register the stdio proxy as an MCP server in ~/.codex/config.toml
[mcp_servers.1mcp]
type = "stdio"
command = "<npm-prefix>/1mcp.cmd"     # or /usr/bin/env 1mcp on Linux
args = ["proxy"]
startup_timeout_sec = 120.0
```

`<npm-prefix>` is `npm bin -g` (e.g. `C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Roaming\npm`).

### Cursor (`~/.cursor/mcp.json` or workspace `mcp.json`)

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "1mcp": { "url": "http://127.0.0.1:3050/mcp?app=cursor" }
  }
}
```

### Claude Code

```bash
# stdio-proxy style (Claude supports stdio natively):
claude mcp add 1mcp "<npm-prefix>/1mcp.cmd" -- proxy
# or repo-scoped CLI hooks:
1mcp cli-setup --claude --scope repo --repo-root .
# or direct HTTP (Claude CLI 1.x+):
claude mcp add -t http 1mcp "http://127.0.0.1:3050/mcp?app=claude-code"
```

### opencode / other stdio clients

Point their stdio MCP launcher at `<npm-prefix>/1mcp.cmd proxy` (Windows) or
`1mcp proxy` (POSIX). opencode does this automatically in its MCP config.

### Tool naming rule (client side)

All backend server tools are surfaced under the 1mcp namespace with the pattern
`{server}_1mcp_{tool}`. In MCP-native clients this lands as
`mcp__1mcp__<server>_1mcp_<tool>` (Codex/Claude) or the client's own flattened
equivalent.Backend server names are the keys you put under `mcpServers` in
`$configDir/mcp.json` (e.g. `codegraph`, `perplexity`, `agent-browser`).

### Session visibility (important)

Most agent clients freeze the MCP tool inventory **at session start**. If
`1mcp serve` is not running when the client spawns its `1mcp proxy` child, the
proxy's MCP `initialize` handshake fails, the client drops the server, and the
session ends up with no `mcp__1mcp__*` tools - **even if you bring `1mcp serve`
up later in that same session, the tool list will not retroactively populate**.
Symptoms: agent flushed with the backends at startup but no 1mcp tools visible;
`1mcp --status` is healthy; only this session is missing tools.

Rule of thumb: bring up `1mcp serve` (service manager or `--background`)**before**
starting the agent session. If you forgot, restart the agent session after the
service is up.

Precise diagnostic signal: when a client probes 1mcp during a session that
connected to a not-yet-bootstrapped daemon, `list_mcp_resources(server:"1mcp")`
(or any `tools/list` call) returns `MCP startup failed: Mcp error: -32603:
Error listing tools ({"originalError":{"code":404}})`. The 404 is **not** a
network failure — `initialize` succeeded but 1mcp failed to enumerate tools.
Two distinct root causes both produce this exact -32603/404 fingerprint:

1. **Stale orphan daemon**: the `server.pid` file points at an old serve
   process that is still listening but whose backend catalog was never built
   fully (e.g. it lost some upstream connections at boot). Fix: kill the
   orphan, delete `server.pid`, restart the scheduled task (`schtasks /end /tn '\1mcp-daemon'; schtasks /run /tn '\1mcp-daemon'`) so it rewrites
   `server.pid` to a fresh healthy daemon.

2. **A single HTTP-backed backend returns its own 404 / -32000**: observed in
   production with `omniroute` (`http://localhost:20128/api/mcp/stream`).
   OmniRoute is a strict Streamable-HTTP MCP server - it maintains its own
   `Mcp-Session-Id` session table; if OmniRoute restarts it forgets the
   session 1mcp is using and replies `{"code":-32000,"message":"Not Found:
   Unknown Mcp-Session-Id header"}` to every upstream call. 1mcp propagates
   that single-backend failure to the entire `tools/list` and returns the
   -32603 404 to the client. Look in `<config-dir>/service-stdout.log` (or
   `logs/server.log`) for `Client <name> error: ... Unknown Mcp-Session-Id
   header` or any `Error listing tools` line to find the offending backend.
   Fix: `1mcp mcp disable <name>` then restart the Task Scheduler task (`schtasks /end /tn '\1mcp-daemon'; schtasks /run /tn '\1mcp-daemon'`) to drop the broken upstream; the remaining 9/10 backends will
   return their tools immediately. Re-enable later once the upstream MCP
   server is restarted and its session table is stable.

Once you see the `-32603 / 404` pair in a session, **the tool table for that
session is frozen** and will not recover - you must restart the agent session
*after* fixing the backend, then verifying `1mcp --status` reports the
correct PID/URL on the **user scope** (`Runtime Scope:
C:\\Users\\<you>\\AppData\\Roaming\\1mcp`).

### Codex App (desktop) stdio channel — empirical decision tree

Observed on Codex App desktop (Windows 11, @1mcp/agent v0.34.4, stdio proxy mode, 10 backends). When a target backend tool (exa, perplexity, etc.) seems "not exposed" in a Codex App session, do NOT conclude the backend is missing. Decision sequence (stop on first hit, mind each step's signal boundary; prefer 1mcp's own CLI for evidence — an empty `tool_search` result is NOT evidence):

1. **Active MCP server check**: 1mcp is "active" in this session only if the Codex App MCP panel shows 1mcp connected, OR `tool_search` in this session can see the `mcp__1mcp__*` namespace. An entry under `[mcp_servers.1mcp]` in `~/.codex/config.toml` is registration only — it does NOT guarantee this session spawned the proxy and can call its tools. If neither signal is visible, go to step 6.
2. **`tool_search` does not pre-enumerate 1mcp child tools**: an empty result is not evidence that "1mcp doesn't have this backend". Invalid signal, skip.
3. **Real naming form**: 1mcp internal qualified name is `<backend>_1mcp_<tool>` (e.g. `exa_1mcp_web_search_exa`, `perplexity_1mcp_pplx_query`); Codex App stacks the `mcp__1mcp__` prefix to give `mcp__1mcp__<backend>_1mcp_<tool>`. Try direct calls in this form. Codex App's stdio MCP channel does NOT guarantee lazy exposure — if the call reports "tool not found", go to step 4.
4. **Codex side not directly callable → 1mcp CLI fallback** for evidence and execution:
   - `1mcp --status` — confirm the aggregated runtime is up (PID + ready).
   - `1mcp mcp list` — list registered backends and confirm the target is enabled.
   - `1mcp inspect <backend> --format json --all` — get real tool names, arg counts, descriptions.
   - `1mcp run <server>/<tool> --args '<json>'` — execute. **Positional format is `<server>/<tool>`, NOT `<qualifiedName>`**; args go through `--args '<json>'`, not `-- <args>`. Passing `1mcp run exa_1mcp_web_search_exa` returns `Tool reference must be in the format <server>/<tool>`.
5. `list_mcp_resources(server:"1mcp")` / `list_mcp_resource_templates(server:"1mcp")` only cover resource-type interfaces, not 1mcp's full tool surface. A miss does not mean the backend is absent; treat as a supplementary signal only.
6. **Fall back** to alternative tools only when 1mcp is not registered in this session AND step 4 has confirmed the backend is genuinely absent. Explain the gap to the user (e.g. "enable 1mcp gateway / add that backend").

Core correction: `tool_search` returning no `mcp__1mcp__*` is NOT evidence that 1mcp is absent or that a backend is missing. Decision order is "confirm this-session activity → direct call by real naming form, on failure fall back to 1mcp CLI", NOT "tool_search hit first, call second".

Empirical confirmation (single run, single host):
- `1mcp --status` → `running (ready)`, PID 2948, URL http://127.0.0.1:3050/mcp.
- `1mcp mcp list` → 10 backends enabled (exa, perplexity included).
- `1mcp inspect exa --format json --all` → `exa_1mcp_web_search_exa`, `exa_1mcp_web_fetch_exa`.
- `1mcp inspect perplexity --format json --all` → `perplexity_1mcp_pplx_query`, `pplx_ask`, `pplx_deep_research`, `pplx_sonar`, `pplx_gpt54`, …
- `1mcp run exa_1mcp_web_search_exa --args '{...}'` → error `Tool reference must be in the format <server>/<tool>`.
- `1mcp run exa/web_search_exa --args '{...}'` → format accepted, exa backend returns its own business error (auth/quota).
- `1mcp run perplexity/pplx_ask --args '{...}'` → format accepted, perplexity backend returns its own auth error.
- `list_mcp_resources(server:"1mcp")` in a session with a stale or unspawned proxy → `MCP startup failed: Mcp error: -32603: Error listing tools ({"originalError":{"code":404}})` (same fingerprint as the "Session visibility" section above).

### CLI mode as a fallback when this session has no `mcp__1mcp__*` tools

When your IDE froze the tool list before the proxy could connect, you can still
utilize the running `1mcp serve` by utilizing the CLI workflow against it:

```bash
1mcp instructions                       # what is loaded + the recommended flow
1mcp inspect context7                  # overview of one backend server
1mcp inspect context7/query-docs       # schema of exactly one tool
1mcp run context7/query-docs --args '{"libraryId":"/mongodb/docs","query":"aggregation pipeline"}'
```

Binaries spawned through your shell here do not go through the per-session MCP
cache, so they always work as long as the serve stays running. This is also
the progressive-discovery surface for agent loops that want minimal token
footprints.

## Common recipes

```bash
# 1) Register a stdio MCP server, then expose the aggregate over stdio
1mcp mcp add context7 -- npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp
1mcp proxy                 # stdio bridge to a running `serve`

# 2) Healthy startup with lazy + async + hot-reload, background daemon
1mcp serve --background \
  --enable-lazy-loading --lazy-mode metatool \
  --enable-async-loading --async-min-servers 2 \
  --enable-config-reload

# 3) Scope servers by preset/filter/tags from .1mcprc
1mcp proxy                                  # reads .1mcprc automatically
1mcp serve --preset my-preset              # or override at serve time
1mcp serve -f "web AND database"           # or via filter expression

# 4) Authenticated runtime
1mcp auth <subcommand>                     # set up profiles first
1mcp serve --enable-auth --enable-scope-validation \
  --rate-limit-window 60 --rate-limit-max 100 --session-ttl 120

# 5) Inspect & run one tool (agent loop)
1mcp instructions
1mcp inspect context7
1mcp inspect context7/query-docs
1mcp run context7/query-docs --args '{"libraryId":"/mongodb/docs","query":"aggregation pipeline"}'

# 6) Status & lifecycle of the selected Runtime Scope
1mcp --status          # report state, exit
1mcp --stop           # stop runtime, exit
1mcp --restart        # stop + fresh restart

# 7) Direct streamable HTTP attachment (MCP-native clients)
#   Cursor:  { "mcpServers": { "1mcp": { "url": "http://127.0.0.1:3050/mcp?app=cursor" } } }
#   Claude:  claude mcp add -t http 1mcp "http://127.0.0.1:3050/mcp?app=claude-code"
```

## Troubleshooting
| Agent session has no `mcp__1mcp__*` tools but `1mcp --status` is healthy | `1mcp serve` was NOT running when the client spawned its `1mcp proxy` at session start; the MCP handshake failed and the tool list froze. Start `1mcp serve` (or confirm the systemd/Task Scheduler unit is up) and restart the agent session. See "Session visibility". |
| `1mcp --status` says not running yet port 3050 is listening | You are running `1mcp --status` as a user whose `%APPDATA%/1mcp` differs from the service account's scope (e.g. LocalSystem service writing into `C:\Windows\System32\config\systemprofile\AppData\Roaming\1mcp`). Use `1mcp --config-dir <that-dir> --status`, or symlink pid files across scopes. |
| Service fails on boot / SCM logs spurious restarts | `serve` default sync loading blocks the HTTP port for ~10-12 s with many backends; if the client retries fast it can trigger a failure counter. Add `--enable-async-loading --async-min-servers 4` so HTTP is ready in ~100 ms. |

| Symptom                                       | Fix                                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `1mcp: command not found` after npm install  | Add `npm bin -g` to PATH, or run via `npx @1mcp/agent <args>`.            |
| Client sees no tools                          | Ensure `1mcp serve` is running (check `1mcp --status`); check `.1mcprc` filter/preset/tags don't exclude all. |
| Too many tools / token bloat                 | Enable `--enable-lazy-loading --lazy-mode metatool`.                       |
| Slow first response                           | Enable `--enable-async-loading --async-min-servers 2`.                     |
| Config not hot-reloading                       | Add `--enable-config-reload --config-reload-debounce 300`. (Also needs file watching to work.) |
| Need OAuth                                     | Use `1mcp auth` profiles + `--enable-auth` (preferred over deprecated `--auth`). |
| Template vars like `{project.path}` literal    | Set the `context` block in `.1mcprc`; proxy must be the entry point.      |
| Server dies when bash command returns         | Use `1mcp serve --background` (detached) or run in a real terminal.        |
| Codex/Claude still flooding tools after setup | Confirm the agent is in CLI mode and old direct MCP config removed.       |
| Two 1mcp daemons at once / 3050 in use or daemon fails to start | An orphan `1mcp serve --background-bootstrap` spawn (cmdline marked `--restart`) may hold 3050, or a stale `runtime.owner\owner.json` + `server.pid` from a killed PID blocks the new serve (`Runtime Scope is already owned by PID N`). Kill the orphan (no service parent) / delete stale `runtime.owner\` + `server.pid`, then restart the scheduled task (`schtasks /end /tn '\1mcp-daemon'; schtasks /run /tn '\1mcp-daemon'`). Verify only one listen socket, verify `1mcp --status` shows the 3050 PID. |
| Port 3050 not listening even though Task Scheduler shows Running | `node.exe` child may have exited during startup. Check `schtasks /query /tn '\1mcp-daemon' /fo LIST /v` for `Last Result`. Verify listener: `Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 3050 -State Listen` and `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -match '1mcp' } | Select ProcessId, CommandLine`. Restart: `schtasks /end /tn '\1mcp-daemon'; schtasks /run /tn '\1mcp-daemon'`. |
| `list_mcp_resources(server:"1mcp")` returns `Mcp error: -32603 ... Error listing tools ... 404` in a new agent session | Two root causes share this fingerprint. (1) `server.pid` points to a stale orphan daemon - kill it, delete `server.pid`, restart the scheduled task (`schtasks /end /tn '\1mcp-daemon'; schtasks /run /tn '\1mcp-daemon'`). (2) A single HTTP-backend (e.g. `omniroute` with its own Mcp-Session-Id table) returns `-32000 Unknown Mcp-Session-Id header` so 1mcp fails the whole `tools/list`. Look in the daemon log for `Client <name> error: ... Unknown Mcp-Session-Id header`, then `1mcp mcp disable <name> then restart the scheduled task (`schtasks /end /tn '\1mcp-daemon'; schtasks /run /tn '\1mcp-daemon'`)` (or the systemd equivalent). See "Session visibility" for the full path. |
| System reboot does not auto-start 1mcp | Verify trigger is `AtStartup` with `StartWhenAvailable=true`: `schtasks /query /tn '\1mcp-daemon' /xml`. Check `RestartOnFailure` has `Count=5` `Interval=PT2M`. After reboot verify: `schtasks /query /tn '\1mcp-daemon'` shows `Running`, `Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 3050 -State Listen`, `Invoke-WebRequest http://127.0.0.1:3050/health/ready` -> 200. |

## Multi-Domain Strategy (CRITICAL for cross-domain queries)
Queries involving multiple domains fall into TWO distinct patterns:

### Pattern 1 — Parallel domains (independent topics per domain)
A single user request asks about DIFFERENT topics in different domains.
Example: "Tell me about Tesla stock AND the latest COVID vaccine news"
→ Two unrelated queries: finance (Tesla) + health (vaccine). Use batch_search with DIFFERENT queries per domain.

### Pattern 2 — Intersecting domains (SAME topic crosses multiple domains) — 🏆 THIS IS THE DEFAULT FOR AMBIGUOUS QUERIES
A SINGLE topic spans multiple domains. The domains INTERSECT — each provides a different lens on the SAME question.
Examples:
  - "AI regulation's impact on healthcare investment" — same topic crosses legal, health, finance
  - "Climate change effects on agricultural supply chains" — same topic crosses environment, agriculture, business
  - "Cryptocurrency's role in cross-border e-commerce" — same topic crosses finance, ecommerce, legal
  - "Space tourism safety regulations and insurance" — same topic crosses travel, legal, finance

**Strategy**: get_sub_domains with ALL intersecting domains, then batch_search — rephrase the SAME core question for each domain's perspective:
  get_sub_domains(domains=["legal", "health", "finance"])
  batch_search(queries=[
    {query:"AI regulation impact on healthcare investment trends 2025", domain:"finance", sub_domain:"finance.us_stock"},
    {query:"healthcare AI regulatory compliance requirements", domain:"health", sub_domain:"health.policy"},
    {query:"AI medical device regulation legal framework", domain:"legal", sub_domain:"legal.legislation"}
  ])

**KEY**: The queries are NOT independent — they all probe the SAME core topic from different domain angles. Do NOT treat intersecting domains as separate unrelated queries.

## Examples
### A — General query (Path 1 — RARE)
User: "what is quantum entanglement"
→ search(query="what is quantum entanglement", max_results=10)

### B — Single-domain vertical (Path 2)
User: "Tesla stock price and latest earnings"
→ get_sub_domains(domains=["finance"])
→ search(query="Tesla stock price earnings", domain="finance", sub_domain="finance.us_stock", sub_domain_params={ticker:"TSLA"}, max_results=10)

### C — Parallel multi-domain (Pattern 1: independent topics per domain)
User: "impact of AI regulation on healthcare stocks in 2025"
→ get_sub_domains(domains=["finance", "health", "legal"])
→ batch_search(queries=[
     {query:"AI regulation impact on healthcare stocks 2025", domain:"finance", sub_domain:"finance.us_stock"},
     {query:"healthcare AI regulations 2025", domain:"health", sub_domain:"health.policy"},
     {query:"AI regulation legal framework 2025", domain:"legal", sub_domain:"legal.legislation"}])
→ extract(url=top_result_url)

### C2 — Intersecting domains (Pattern 2: SAME topic viewed through multiple domain lenses)
User: "Cryptocurrency mining's environmental impact and regulatory response"
→ Single topic (crypto mining) intersecting environment, energy, finance, legal. Cover all angles.
→ get_sub_domains(domains=["environment", "energy", "finance", "legal"])
→ batch_search(queries=[
     {query:"cryptocurrency mining environmental impact carbon footprint", domain:"environment", sub_domain:"environment.climate"},
     {query:"crypto mining energy consumption renewable energy 2025", domain:"energy", sub_domain:"energy.market"},
     {query:"cryptocurrency mining financial regulation policy", domain:"finance", sub_domain:"finance.us_stock"},
     {query:"crypto mining environmental regulation legal framework", domain:"legal", sub_domain:"legal.legislation"}])

### D — Hybrid example 1: classical text + modern application
User: "What is 'The Art of War' and its influence on modern business?"
→ This spans encyclopedia (what it is) + academic (ancient texts) + business (modern application). Hybrid.
→ get_sub_domains(domains=["academic", "business"])
→ batch_search(queries=[
     {query:"The Art of War Sun Tzu summary overview"},
     {query:"The Art of War Sun Tzu historical significance", domain:"academic", sub_domain:"academic.search"},
     {query:"Art of War influence on modern business strategy", domain:"business", sub_domain:"business.market_research"}])

### E — Hybrid example 2: financial concept + current data
User: "What is quantitative easing and how is it being used in 2025?"
→ Encyclopedia definition + current financial data. Cover both.
→ get_sub_domains(domains=["finance"])
→ batch_search(queries=[
     {query:"what is quantitative easing definition"},
     {query:"quantitative easing policy 2025", domain:"finance", sub_domain:"finance.us_stock"}])

## Path 2 triggers (use vertical routing when the query has these signals):
- Structured identifiers: ticker, DOI, CVE, IATA, coordinates, patent number
- Specialized verticals: stock price, flight status, paper search, drug info, weather, exchange rate, geo POI, AQI
- Places / locations / addresses / directions → geo domain
- Borderline encyclopedia topics with strong domain overlap (classical texts → academic/business, financial theories → finance, legal concepts → legal, medical conditions → health) — consider hybrid (Path 1 + Path 2 via batch_search) for richer coverage
- Ambiguous / fuzzy queries — when unsure, hybrid general+vertical via batch_search is the safest option

## Path 1 triggers (use general search directly, no get_sub_domains):
- News, current events, latest updates without a structured identifier
- People, companies, products, places without needing structured fields
- Concept explanations, opinions, comparisons, URL verification, fact-checking
- Any quick lookup where you do not need a domain-specific data source

## CRITICAL Rules:
⛔ NEVER call search with domain/sub_domain/sub_domain_params unless get_sub_domains was called first in this context.
- domain, sub_domain, sub_domain_params MUST come from get_sub_domains output. NEVER guess.
- query is pure natural language. Structured params → sub_domain_params, NEVER in query.
- ONE intent per search call. Split multi-intent queries with batch_search.
- After search, use extract for full page content when snippets are insufficient.
- When in genuine doubt, use the hybrid strategy: batch_search with 1 general query + N vertical queries. Coverage > guessing.
- When using Path 2, prefer get_sub_domains(domains=[...]) with multiple domains if the query could match more than one vertical.
- Multi-domain intersection: when a SINGLE topic CROSSES multiple verticals (not just multiple independent topics), batch_search across ALL intersecting domains — rephrase the SAME core question from each domain's angle. See Multi-Domain Strategy section.

## Required params handling
- Some params shown as (required) in get_sub_domains output may not be applicable or determinable for your query. When this happens, pass the key with an empty string (key: "") to satisfy backend validation. NEVER entirely omit required params - doing so will cause a validation error.",

      "optionalArgs": 4
    }
  ],
  "totalTools": 4,
  "hasMore": false
}
